Reference / io/buffer

io/buffer#

Bytes in memory, read, written and observed through separate views.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let buffer = ByteBuffer();
buffer.writing() <- "hello" <- [byte(255)];
let prefix = buffer.reading().bytes(2);       // consumed
let rest = buffer.content().bytes();          // a snapshot, not consumed
buffer.closing().close();

Description#

Bytes in memory, read, written and observed through separate views.

Every view shares one store. Reading consumes from the front, writing appends, BufferContent shows what is unread without consuming it, and its bytes() is an independent copy. flush() has nothing to do. close() is idempotent, frees the bytes and makes every view refuse with ClosedBuffer.

There is no text buffer here: write text with writing() <- text, read lines with Utf8Input(origin: buffer.reading()), or build text with strings/buffer's TextBuffer.
